examples.text: The seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord.

glosses: A very large meal, often of a ceremonial nature.

examples.text: We had a feast to celebrate the harvest.

glosses: Something delightful

examples.text: It was a feast for the eyes.

glosses: To partake in a feast, or large meal.

examples.text: I feasted on turkey and dumplings.

glosses: To dwell upon (something) with delight.

examples.text: With my love's picture then my eye doth feast.

glosses: To hold a feast in honor of (someone).

examples.text:
He that shall see this day, and live old age,
Will yearly on the vigil feast his neighbors
And say “Tomorrow is Saint Crispian.”
His ancestor, he said, had been feasted there, when he went forward with the then Lord Ravenswood to the fatal battle of Flodden, in which they both fell.
We feasted them after the victory.

examples.text:

glosses: To negotiate, discuss terms, bargain (for or with).

examples.text: Now halting a few paces before the Captains of the West he looked them up and down and laughed. 'Is there any in this rout with authority to treat with me?' he asked.
After all, in this hideous war we have just passed through never forget that Halifax would have treated with Hitler: it took Churchill to refuse.

glosses: To discourse; to handle a subject in writing or speaking; to conduct a discussion.

examples.text: Cicero's writing treats mainly of old age and personal duty.
Now of love they treat.

And, indeed, should the excellent Mr Broughton be prevailed on to set fist to paper, and to complete the above-said rudiments, by delivering down the true principles of athletics, I question whether the world will have any cause to lament, that none of the great writers, either antient or modern, have ever treated about that noble and useful art.
Rhetoric includes the earliest known theory on the proper use of metaphor; On Poetics treats the role of symbolism in drama and poetry.

glosses: To discourse on; to represent or deal with in a particular way, in writing or speaking.

examples.text: The article treated feminism as a quintessentially modern movement.

glosses: To entreat or beseech (someone).

examples.text: Only let my family live, I treat thee.
To treate a tiran it is but thing in vayne.

glosses: To handle, deal with or behave towards in a specific way.

examples.text: You treated me like a fool.
She was tempted to treat the whole affair as a joke.

glosses: To entertain with food or drink, especially at one's own expense; to show hospitality to; to pay for as celebration or reward.

examples.text: My husband treated me to a Paris holiday for our anniversary.
I treated my son to some popcorn in the interval.
I've done so well this month, I'll treat you all to dinner (or Dinner is my treat.)

glosses: To commit the offence of providing food, drink, entertainment or provision to corruptly influence a voter.
To care for medicinally or surgically; to apply medical care to.

examples.text: They treated me for malaria.
We treated firefighters suffering from smoke inhalation, giving them oxygen to breathe and albuterol mist to help open their airways.

glosses: To subject to a chemical or other action; to act upon with a specific scientific result in mind.

examples.text: I treated the photo somewhat to make the colours more pronounced.
He treated the substance with sulphuric acid.

glosses: To provide (someone) with something special and pleasant.

examples.text: If good acting in movies is appealing and you enjoy live performances of theatre, you may soon be treated by the GMC's own endeavors in the theatrical arts.

The Chelsea captain was a virtual spectator as he was treated to his side's biggest win for almost two years as Stamford Bridge serenaded him with chants of "there's only one England captain," some 48 hours after he announced his retirement from international football.

glosses: An entertainment, outing, food, drink, or other indulgence provided by someone for the enjoyment of others.

examples.text: I took the kids to the zoo for a treat.

glosses: An unexpected gift, event etc., which provides great pleasure.

examples.text: It was such a treat to see her back in action on the London stage.
